label: US Unemployment Rate
delta: Unchanged vs July (4.1%); NFP beat consensus by ~3x
deltaNote: AUG 2026 (Sept 4): NFP rose 162,000 — a large beat vs the ~53,000-56,000 gain expected — with June and July both revised up a combined 55,000. Unemployment held steady at 4.1%. Markets read the report as increasing Fed hike risk (CME odds to ~58%), reversing Fed Governor Waller's dovish Sept 3 signal within a day; the Dow, S&P 500, and Nasdaq all fell on the print. label: US PCE Inflation (July 2026)
source: BEA Personal Income and Outlays, July 2026 (released August 26, 2026)
delta: Core flat vs June (3.3%); headline +0.1pp above consensus
deltaNote: JULY 2026 (released Aug 26): Headline PCE 3.7% YoY (+0.2% MoM), 0.1pp above the Dow Jones consensus. Core PCE 3.3% YoY (+0.2% MoM), matching consensus and flat vs June's 3.3% (down from May's cycle-high 3.4%). Personal income +0.4% MoM; spending +0.2% MoM; saving rate 3.0%. Warsh cited these exact 3.7%/4.1% (12mo/6mo) readings in his Aug 28 Jackson Hole keynote as evidence 'underlying trends have [not] meaningfully improved,' noting 54% of the consumption basket is still rising faster than 3% — a key justification for the hawkish tilt that pushed September hike odds to 57%.

label: Fed Funds Rate
value: 3.50–3.75%; September 15-16 Hike Odds ~87% After Hot August CPI/PPI Cemented the Case for a Hike
source: Federal Reserve FOMC, July 29 2026 (held); BLS PPI (Sept 10) and CPI (Sept 11) August releases; CME FedWatch, Sept 11 2026
delta: +29pp — hike odds jumped from ~58% (Sept 4) to ~70% (pre-CPI, Sept 10-11) to ~87% after the Sept 11 core CPI beat
deltaNote: SEPT 8-11 ARC: Canada's $27.6B retaliatory tariffs took effect Sept 8, adding a fresh trade-friction input. The Aug PPI (Sept 10) showed wholesale inflation accelerating to 5.4% YoY, over three-quarters of the rise from energy (diesel +24.1%) as the Gulf oil shock fed into producer prices; the 10Y Treasury hit a 4.969% cycle high the same day as Brent topped $105-107, its highest in nearly four months. The Aug CPI (Sept 11) then ran hot on core — 0.3% MoM (0.1pp above forecast), 2.4% YoY in line — even though headline (3.4% YoY, 0.4% MoM) matched consensus. CME FedWatch hike odds for the Sept 15-16 FOMC jumped to ~87% (from ~70% pre-CPI), with Nationwide's Kathy Bostjancic noting Warsh's condition for a hold — continued disinflation — was not met. Equities rallied Sept 11 (Dow +1.03%, S&P +1.07%, Nasdaq +1.23%) as oil pulled back, ending a four-session slide. Prior: Waller's Sept 3 dovish remarks briefly cut odds to ~48-55%; the Sept 4 jobs blowout (+162K vs +53K expected) reversed that to ~58%.

label: US 10Y / 30Y Treasury Yield
value: 10Y at ~4.97% (Sept 10) — New Cycle High, Highest Since October 2023, as Oil Topped $105 and PPI Ran Hot
source: CNBC / Federal Reserve H.15 / FRED / Yahoo Finance; July 23 - September 10, 2026
delta: +0.18pp since Sept 4 (4.79% → 4.969%) as the Aug PPI print (5.4% YoY) and a fresh oil surge (Brent >$105) pushed the 10Y to its firmest level since October 2023
deltaNote: SEPT 4-10 ARC: The Sept 4 jobs blowout sent the 10Y back to 4.79%, near its Sept 2 cycle high, as CME hike odds rose to ~58%. Yields kept climbing into the new week: a fourth straight losing session for stocks on Sept 9 came alongside the 10Y touching its highest level since 2023 even after Treasury Secretary Bessent unveiled a $6B bond buyback plan aimed at supporting liquidity. The move culminated Sept 10 when the Aug PPI showed wholesale inflation accelerating to 5.4% YoY (energy +4.2%, diesel +24.1%) on the Gulf conflict's oil shock — the same day Brent topped $105-107/bbl (highest in ~4 months) and diesel hit a record $5.94/gal — sending the 10Y to roughly 4.97%, its firmest level since October 2023. The Sept 11 CPI (core 0.3% MoM, hot) pushed Fed hike odds to ~87%, though yields eased modestly as oil pulled back and stocks rallied. The 30-year's Aug 17 peak of 5.31-5.32% (highest since June 2007) remains the cycle high for that tenor. National debt concerns (nearing $40T), stubborn above-target inflation, and the unresolved US-Iran Gulf conflict remain the structural floor under long-end yields heading into the Sept 16-17 FOMC.

label: Michigan Consumer Sentiment (August 2026 Final)
delta: +0.7 vs preliminary (51.0); still -6.3% vs July final (55.2)
deltaNote: AUG 2026 FINAL (released Aug 28): 51.7, revised up from the 51.0 preliminary but still down 6.3% from July's final 55.2 and roughly 11% below a year ago. Current Economic Conditions fell 5.3% to 51.9; Consumer Expectations fell 7.0% to 51.5. One-year inflation expectations eased to 4.0% (from 4.2% preliminary); long-run expectations held at 3.3% for a third straight month. Sentiment fell across all political groups, sharpest among Republicans, older consumers, and lower/middle-income households. Still well above May 2026's all-time record low of 44.8, but the reading — alongside July retail sales' steepest drop in over a year — underscores the crack in the 'resilient consumer' narrative that Warsh's same-day hawkish Jackson Hole keynote did nothing to ease.

label: S&P 500 / Market Risk Gauge
value: S&P 500 at 7,672.80 (Sept 11) — Rebounded 1.07% to End a Four-Session Slide as Oil Cooled and CPI Read 'In Line Enough'
source: AP / Yahoo Finance / CNBC / TheStreet / Federal Reserve; July 23 – September 11, 2026
delta: -45.8 vs Sept 4 close (7,718.60 → 7,672.80) over the week, but +1.07% on Sept 11 alone as the index snapped a four-day losing streak
deltaNote: SEPT 4-11 ARC: The Sept 4 jobs blowout left the S&P 500 at 7,718.60, within ~1% of its record high. From there, a synchronized rise in oil (Brent toward $105-107 by Sept 10, highest in ~4 months) and Treasury yields (10Y to a fresh ~4.97% cycle high) drove a four-session slide into Sept 10, when the S&P closed around 7,592 (Dow ~52,064, Nasdaq ~26,082), down roughly 0.6% each on the day. The Aug PPI (Sept 10, +5.4% YoY) compounded the pressure. Sept 11 reversed the slide sharply: the Aug CPI's headline (3.4% YoY, 0.4% MoM) matched consensus even though core ran hot, and — combined with oil pulling back from its Sept 10 high — stocks rallied hard: Dow +1.03% to 52,602.74, S&P 500 +1.07% to 7,672.80, Nasdaq +1.23% to 26,403.77. The net effect: CME Fed hike odds for Sept 15-16 surged to ~87%, yet equities read the week as resolving uncertainty rather than raising it, closing essentially flat for the week despite the intraweek volatility.

contestNote: Canada's counter-tariffs on roughly $27.6B of US goods took effect at 12:01am Sept 8, tiered at 15%/25%/50% by product (steel, aluminum, furniture, clothing at 50%; dairy, seafood, appliances at 25%; other industrial goods at 15%), largely matching the corresponding US Section 338 rate. The Section 338 tariffs themselves (50% on ~$20B of Canadian autos, alcohol, and dairy) have been in force since Aug 22, after US-Canada trade talks collapsed. Trump's Aug 24 threat of additional 50% tariffs on Canadian autos, auto parts, and steel from Jan 1, 2027 remains outstanding. Separately, the Section 122/Section 301 transition (60 economies, 10-12.5%) that resolved July 24 remains in force; USMCA-qualifying goods stay exempt from Section 301.

source: China NBS (Jul 14 / Aug 17 / Sept 8, 2026) / IMF WEO Jul 2026 / Reuters / CNBC
contestNote: Q2 2026 missed forecast (4.3% vs 4.5% expected), down from 5.0% in Q1 — slowest pace in roughly 3.5 years. July activity data (Aug 17) extended the slowdown: industrial output +4.5% YoY (missed forecast); retail sales +0.6% (missed forecast); Jan-Jul fixed-asset investment -6.7%. August trade data (Sept 8) is a mixed signal for the recovery debate: exports jumped 25% YoY to $401.44B (autos +43%, semiconductors +129.8%) on AI-driven global demand, pushing the trade surplus to a record $119.09B, but imports rose only 28.2% YoY versus a ~30% forecast — evidence domestic demand remains soft even as exports do the heavy lifting. Beijing's late-July Politburo pledge of 'targeted stimulus' has yet to translate into major new measures.

deltaNote: Q1 2026: 5.0% (front-loaded exports). Q2 2026: 4.3% — Iran war demand destruction and property-sector drag materializing as expected. July's across-the-board activity miss (Aug 17) reinforced the structural-slowdown case. Sept 8 trade data shows exports remain the primary growth engine (redirected increasingly to Southeast Asia, Latin America, and Africa to offset US tariffs) while the import miss confirms household demand has not recovered, keeping pressure on Beijing for stronger H2 fiscal support.

label: BOJ Policy Rate
source: Bank of Japan, June 16 2026 (25bp hike — highest since 1995)
deltaNote: June 16: BOJ hiked 25bp to 1.00%, the highest level since 1995, in a 7-1 vote (Asada dissenting) — citing Iran-war energy-cost pass-through risk. The hike landed the same day Warsh's first FOMC opened, raising August-2024-style carry-unwind concerns; the immediate market reaction was orderly (Nikkei +0.46%), but the yen still fell to a fresh 40-year low past 162/USD by June 30 despite the hike and an estimated $72.5bn in prior FX intervention.
